newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada/Europe canola price spread seen narrowing.
newsitem.headline: Canada/Europe canola price spread seen narrowing.

text.p: A US$30 per tonne spread between Canadian and European canola seed values began to narrow 10 days ago and was likely to continue converging when South America's soybean harvest is complete, XCan Grain Ltd's senior trader Joachim Toens told a Canadian Wheat Board conference here Monday.
"European seed values came up US$7 to US$8 a tonne from being US$30 a tonne below Canadian prices in the last 10 days," Toens told Reuters after his speech.

High Canadian canola values would likely result in an increase of as much as 40 percent in seeded acreage on Canada's Prairies this spring which could result in production reaching 7.0 million tonnes in crop year 1997/98 (Aug/July), he told conference delegates.
Even with a near-record domestic crush in the coming crop year of 2.7 million tonnes, projected ending stocks of 1.4 million tonnes would weigh on prices, he added.

"We arrive at a carry-out of 1.4 million tonnes and a stocks to use ratio of 23 percent. This is too high. It becomes evident that more Canadian canola will have to find a home in export markets," Toens said.

Canola values in the coming weeks would likely track soybean prices very closely until South America's soybean crops are harvested, he said. Then the price gap between Canada and Europe should converge further.

"Once the South American crops are safe, I do believe the new crop canola will have to separate from the beans and find its own value, which might well be lower for the new crop, as much as US$30 per tonne as mentioned earlier due to the need to be competitive on world markets," Toens said.
"The old crop is a different ballgame, as the relatively tight (1996/97) carry-out (at 368,000 tonnes) indicates the inverse might be justified, or even too small," he added.
